issues.failure_explanation: The cross term -(2/gamma)|a_h^E(psi,varphi)| is first bounded by (2/gamma)c^*||grad psi|| ||grad varphi||, using the upper stability constant, while the diagonal terms only keep the lower constant c_*. Positivity of both gradient coefficients then needs eps_4 > c^*/(gamma c_*) and eps_4 < c_*/c^*. The interval is nonempty only if 1/gamma < (c_*/c^*)^2 <= 1. The hypothesis 0 < 1/gamma < 1 does not give this, and c_*, c^* depend on the stabilization. The same restriction appears in the 'similarly' case 1/gamma > 1, where one needs 1/gamma > (c^*/c_*)^2. The displayed choice of eps_4 is therefore not generally possible, and (3.9) is not proved for all gamma in the stated regime.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply Cauchy-Schwarz to the symmetric semi-definite form a_h^E directly, |a_h^E(psi,varphi)| <= a_h^E(psi,psi)^{1/2} a_h^E(varphi,varphi)^{1/2}. Then use that 1/gamma^2 < 1/gamma (resp. 1 < 1/gamma) gives coercivity in the a_h-seminorm, and only afterwards convert to H^1 norms with c_*, c^*.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete Garding/T-coercivity (3.9) is unproved for 1/gamma close to 1 (or to 1 from above) or for badly scaled stabilizations. Lemma 3.4 uses (3.9) directly, and the eigenvalue and eigenfunction theorems use Lemma 3.4.
issues.title: Discrete T-coercivity proof needs 1/gamma < (c_*/c^*)^2, which is not guaranteed
issues.why_classification: A short local change in the Young-inequality step fixes the proof; the statement, constants and all downstream results are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: by Fredholm's alternative we conclude that the problem \eqref{a3.5} is well-posed

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 3.1 gives only a Garding-type inequality with an extra K||.||_W^2 term. On a finite-dimensional space, Fredholm's alternative yields solvability only if the homogeneous discrete problem is injective. Injectivity is argued from the claim that 'k_h^2 converges to k^2', which misreads a fixed parameter as a convergent discrete eigenvalue. It is supported only by a citation to a different (anisotropic Helmholtz) VEM problem and is not shown for the present indefinite, non-selfadjoint, stabilized form a_h. No argument is given for an h-independent bound, so the constant in (3.11) is unestablished.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a lemma showing injectivity of a_h on V_h for h small, with an h-uniform inf-sup bound. For example, combine T-coercivity with discrete compactness, or a Schatz-type argument using the consistency estimates and the continuous well-posedness. Then derive (3.11).
issues.overall_effect: Existence and uniqueness of U_h^F for small h, the definition of A_h, and the uniform stability used by the duality and absorption arguments (Lemmas 3.3-3.4) and by the spectral theory are not rigorously established. The abstract's claim of well-posedness of the discrete source problem is unsupported.
issues.title: Discrete well-posedness and h-uniform stability (3.11) asserted without valid argument
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial new lemma is needed; the overall framework and rates survive, so the loss is not major.

issues.failure_explanation: The discrete source problem (3.5) uses b_h(F,.) for F in W=L^2xL^2, but b_h involves Pi^0 and the stabilization S_b through degrees of freedom, which are undefined for general L^2 data f. The proof of (3.18) nevertheless evaluates S_b^E((I-Pi^0)f,...) for such f. The operator A_h is instead defined with the exact form b(F,.), so the term b-b_h analysed in Lemma 3.3 does not arise for the operator actually defined. Moreover, the discrete eigenproblem (3.3) uses b_h, so A_h U_{j,h} = U_{j,h}/(beta-lambda_{j,h}) is false for the A_h defined with b, since b_h differs from b on V_h. Hence the eigenvalue problem (3.3) is not the eigenproblem of the A_h analysed, and Babuska-Osborn theory is applied to a different operator.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define A_h on V_h (or on smooth data) via b_h(F_I,.) with an interpolant or projection of the data, so that eigenpairs of (3.3) are exactly eigenpairs of A_h. Then redo the consistency terms in Lemmas 3.3-3.4 and the operator-norm convergence with this operator, handling the data-interpolation error.
issues.overall_effect: Lemmas 3.3-3.4, the operator-norm convergence claims, and the eigenspace, eigenvalue and eigenfunction estimates are derived for objects that are either undefined for L^2 data or not the operator tied to (3.3).
issues.title: Discrete source problem and operator A_h inconsistent (b vs b_h); b_h undefined for L^2 data
issues.why_classification: The consistency analysis must be redone for a corrected operator, but the same estimates and rates are expected to survive, so it is a contained reconstruction rather than new global architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: assuming that the ascent of the eigenvalue $\lambda_j$ is 1

issues.failure_explanation: The h^{2 min(l,s)} bound proved in Theorem 3.1 holds only for the arithmetic mean hat-lambda_{j,h} of the q discrete eigenvalues near lambda_j. The theorem assumes only ascent 1, not that lambda_j is simple (the numerical examples have double eigenvalues). For an individual lambda_{j,h} with q>1, the general Babuska-Osborn bound is of the same order as the eigenvector error, so the claim that |lambda_{j,h}-lambda_j| is small compared with ||U_j-U_{j,h}||_V is unsupported. Hence the step in (3.35) is not justified, and the cited Theorem 7.3 and (3.28)-(3.29) do not provide it.

failure_location.quote: we know that $|\lambda_{j,h}-\lambda_j|$ is a small quantity compared to

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State (3.31) with ||(A_h-A)U_j||_V (or its O(h^{min(l,s)}) bound from Lemma 3.4) on the right-hand side. Alternatively, restrict to simple eigenvalues or use an eigenvalue-error bound valid for the individual eigenvalue.
issues.overall_effect: Only the refined L^2 estimate (3.31) is affected; (3.29) and (3.30) follow directly from the cited abstract results.
issues.title: Unjustified absorption of |lambda_{j,h}-lambda_j| in (3.35) for individual (possibly multiple) eigenvalues
issues.why_classification: A local rewording of the right-hand side of (3.31), or an added simplicity hypothesis, keeps the stated rates; the main conclusions are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Nevertheless, on finer meshes, both VEM and FEM achieve at least 5 to 6 digits of accuracy in their approximations.
The first four approximate eigenvalues obtained by VEM and FEM on the $(b)$-type mesh generation of $\Omega_C$.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims, from Figures 3-5 and Table 5, that VEM beats FEM on irregular meshes. FEM is run only on the regular triangular mesh (b), where the l=1 results coincide exactly with VEM; Figures 3-5 are VEM-only, so no FEM-versus-VEM comparison on irregular meshes exists. The claimed 5-6 digit accuracy has no reference values for the disk, and the reported values do not support it. Finest-mesh lambda_1 is -1.72626633 (l=1, b), -1.72676450 (l=2, b) and -1.72574838 (l=2, a), which differ in the third or fourth digit, while the l=2 sequences decrease by factors of about 4 rather than 16.

failure_location.quote: we find that VEM has an advantage over FEM when handling

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove or weaken the claims, or add FEM computations on irregular meshes and reference eigenvalues for the disk, with an accounting of polygonal domain-approximation error.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical section's comparative conclusions and accuracy statements are not established by the data shown; the theoretical results are unaffected.
issues.title: Concluding VEM-vs-FEM and accuracy claims not supported by the reported experiments
issues.why_classification: This is an unsupported remark in the numerical discussion; deleting or qualifying it leaves the theory and the main numerical verification intact.
